questions.q: What field turns on streaming in a Messages API request?
questions.explain: Setting stream to true switches the response to server-sent events instead of one JSON blob.

options: Perceived latency — time to the first visible token
questions.explain: Total time to the last token is about the same; streaming mainly improves how soon the user sees something happening.

questions.q: In Anthropic's streaming sequence, what does a content_block_delta event carry?
options: A small incremental fragment of content, like a piece of text
The entire message in one shot
A keep-alive signal with no data
questions.explain: Each content_block_delta carries one small delta — for text, a text_delta fragment appended to the running content block.

questions.q: Which Anthropic event carries the final stop_reason and completed usage counts?
questions.explain: message_delta arrives near the end of the stream with the final stop_reason and usage totals, just before message_stop.

questions.q: How does OpenAI's Chat Completions API signal the end of a stream?
options: A dedicated message_stop event, same as Anthropic
The connection simply closes with no marker
questions.explain: OpenAI's stream ends with a literal [DONE] sentinel sent as the final data line, rather than Anthropic's named message_stop event.
